title: Why Is My Washing Machine Leaking From Underneath?

seo.title: Why Is My Washing Machine Leaking From Underneath?
seo.meta_description: If water appears under the washer, dry the floor and identify whether the leak begins during fill, wash, or drain. Stop if water reaches electrical parts.
seo.search_intent: Locate a washer leak by cycle stage and distinguish external hoses or drains from internal failures that require repair.

excerpt: The puddle ends up underneath, but the source may be higher on the machine. When the leak starts — fill, wash, or drain — is one of the best clues.
content_html:
Stop the washer, shut off the water supply if the leak is active, and stay clear of water around electrical connections. Then dry the floor so fresh moisture is easier to trace.

If it leaks while filling, inspect the inlet hoses

Look for water at the shutoff valves, hose fittings, and hose surfaces. A leak at the back can run down the cabinet and emerge underneath.

If it leaks while washing, check the door and suds

On front-load machines, debris or damage at the door boot can let water escape. Excess detergent can create foam that leaks from vents or the dispenser area.

If it leaks while draining, follow the drain path

Inspect the accessible drain hose and standpipe. A household drain restriction can overflow even when the washer itself is not leaking internally.

Do not tip or dismantle a water-filled washer

Pumps, clamps, tubs, and internal seals require safe access. If water appears from the center underside while all external connections stay dry, service is the sensible next step.

Do not resume normal use until the source is resolved; even a small repeated leak can damage flooring and electrical components.

faq.question: Does a puddle underneath mean the tub is cracked?
faq.answer: No. Inlet hoses, drains, the door seal, or dispenser can leak and send water underneath.

faq.question: Should I run another cycle to find the source?
faq.answer: Only if the leak is very small and there is no electrical risk. Stop immediately for a significant active leak.

faq.question: What if water reached the outlet?
faq.answer: Do not touch wet electrical connections. Isolate power from a safe location and get qualified help.
